_about: Organisations that make up the Spokane-area tech and startup scene — investors, accelerators, coworking spaces, groups, events and spaces — researched from public sources 2026-10-03. Every entry carries its sources and the most recent dated sign it is still running. lng/lat are present only where the organisation has a sourced street address; a meetup or a fund without one has no pin.
_excluded: Researched and left out: Barton Ventures and Tacoma Venture Fund (out-of-area investors, one Spokane deal each); SEEN (not tech-focused); Innovator Connect (no session since January 2025); Urbanova and INTENT (merged into Novara); SP3NW (defunct); Founders Live Spokane (no event since February 2024); Women Who Code (dissolved 2024); Spokane Linux User Group and Agile and Lean Spokane (inactive); Coeur d'Alene groups and events (outside the map).

organisations.name: Spokane Angel Alliance
organisations.what: Angel network of more than 100 individual and institutional members, managed by Ignite Northwest, investing in emerging companies across Eastern Washington, Idaho and Montana. Startups that pitched to it raised a combined $26.4M in 2025.
organisations.focus: Emerging companies in Eastern Washington, Idaho and Montana

organisations.name: Kick-Start Seed Funds
organisations.what: Series of regional angel and venture funds managed by Ignite Northwest. Kick-Start V closed at $3.8M in 2023, and the funds have put $11M into 51 companies through 2025.
organisations.focus: $100K–$500K in equity or convertible notes; mostly Spokane, Coeur d'Alene and Sandpoint
organisations.lastActive: Co-invested in Gestalt Diagnostics' Series A, April 2025

organisations.name: Ignite Northwest
organisations.what: Spokane nonprofit that funds, mentors and accelerates fast-growing regional companies. It runs loan funds — $12M across 33 companies through 2025 — manages Kick-Start and the Spokane Angel Alliance, and publishes the annual 25+5 list.
organisations.focus: Loans of $100K–$500K for startups that cannot get bank credit

organisations.name: Cowles Ventures
organisations.what: Venture arm of Spokane's Cowles Co., investing directly in startups and through managed funds. It developed and runs FUEL Coworking downtown.
organisations.lastActive: Led Gestalt Diagnostics' $7.5M Series A, April 2025

organisations.name: Avista Development
organisations.what: Subsidiary of Avista Corp. investing in early-stage companies with energy-industry products, such as the wildfire-defence startup Blaze Barrier.
organisations.lastActive: Invested in Blaze Barrier's seed round, reported April 2026

organisations.name: Big Horn Ventures
organisations.what: Investor that led XpenseOne's seed round in December 2017.
organisations.lastActive: Led XpenseOne's seed round, December 2017 — no later Spokane deal found

organisations.name: InnovateINW
organisations.what: The regional innovation initiative of LaunchPad Inland Northwest (launchpadinw.com now redirects here). Runs the Springboard founder-coaching programme, Springboard Scale, an AI & Cyber Network and regular ecosystem events.
organisations.focus: Clean tech, AI and robotics, cybersecurity, advanced manufacturing, bio and health sciences
organisations.lastActive: AI ecosystem event, 23 July 2026; Pitch Jam, 8 October 2026

organisations.name: Health Sciences & Services Authority (HSSA)
organisations.what: Spokane County public development authority giving grants for bioscience-based economic development and access to care, through programmes including RD&C Spokane and Spokane Early Stage.
organisations.focus: Bioscience and health startups; Level II matching grants up to $750K
organisations.lastActive: $3.25M in Level II grants to five startups, April 2026

organisations.name: Evergreen Bioscience Innovation Cluster
organisations.what: Nonprofit life-science cluster, formed with Greater Spokane Inc., running a 5,000 sq ft incubator with wet-lab and office space in a former Neogen facility.

organisations.name: Riverside Biotech Hub
organisations.what: Downtown life-science incubator opened in 2025, with shared wet lab, offices, coworking and equipment access for early-stage biotech startups.
organisations.lastActive: Cited as active by the Spokane Journal, May 2026

organisations.name: StartUp Spokane
organisations.what: Free business-resource hub from Spokane Public Library and Spokane County Library District: business-librarian consultations, mentors, and premium research databases and planning tools.

organisations.name: Gonzaga Hogan Entrepreneurial Leadership Program
organisations.what: Gonzaga's honours entrepreneurship programme, founded in 2000, including the student-run New Venture Lab that consults for local entrepreneurs.
organisations.lastActive: Partner in a Spokane entrepreneur programme launched September 2025

organisations.name: Novara Energy Alliance
organisations.what: Energy-innovation nonprofit formed in 2026 from the merger of Urbanova and INTENT, backed by Avista, Itron and McKinstry, bringing industry, researchers, founders and investors together on energy and water problems.
organisations.focus: Grid modernisation, energy resilience, clean energy

organisations.name: FUEL Coworking
organisations.what: Downtown coworking for startups, freelancers and remote teams, developed by Cowles Ventures: hot desks, dedicated desks, private offices and event space. Hosts many of the scene's events.

organisations.name: Burbity Workspaces
organisations.what: Locally owned coworking with four locations — Liberty Lake, Sprague/University District, Sullivan Valley Commons and South Hill — offering desks, offices, meeting rooms and event space.

organisations.name: Fellow Coworking
organisations.what: Downtown shared office and coworking space in the Washington Cracker Co. building, open since 2013, with drop-in, hot-desk, permanent-desk and virtual memberships.

organisations.name: Spokane Python User Group
organisations.what: Spokane's Python user group, covering Python, web development and open source, hosted by IntelliTect.
organisations.cadence: Talks around the third Tuesday monthly; Coffee & Code on the first Monday at 7am

organisations.name: Spokane .NET Users Group
organisations.what: User group for developers and architects working with Microsoft .NET, affiliated with the .NET Foundation and hosted by IntelliTect, with hybrid meetings and an annual .NET Conf.

organisations.name: Spokane DevOps Meetup
organisations.what: Mostly online meetup on DevOps, automation, cloud and deployment, sponsored by IntelliTect.

organisations.name: Spokane Go Users Group
organisations.what: Community for the Go programming language and software development generally: a little mingling, then a talk.
organisations.lastActive: Joint meetup with the Python group, 22 September 2026

organisations.name: Spokane Tech Community
organisations.what: Meetup for people in the Spokane area who work in tech, used to, or are training for it — project showcases, discussions and socials.

organisations.name: SpokaneTech.org
organisations.what: Volunteer community site and calendar listing the Inland Northwest's tech groups and their upcoming events, with a shared Discord.

organisations.name: Spokane UX
organisations.what: Community of user-experience professionals and learners meeting for talks and socials.

organisations.name: DC509
organisations.what: Spokane's DEF CON group, active since 2010: hacking, network security, hardware hacking and secure coding, for beginners and professionals.

organisations.name: INCH360
organisations.what: Inland Northwest Cyber Hub: a regional group connecting cybersecurity and compliance professionals, which runs an annual free security and AI conference.

organisations.name: Spokane AI
organisations.what: Organiser of the Spokane AI Mixer, networking for data scientists, computer scientists and machine-learning practitioners.

organisations.name: Spokane WordPress Meetup
organisations.what: Local group of WordPress developers, designers and publishers running WordPress Wednesday help desks and socials.

organisations.name: GDG on Campus EWU
organisations.what: Eastern Washington University's student Google Developer Group: ML workshops, tech hangouts and the Build With AI hackathon.

organisations.name: INTERFACE Spokane
organisations.what: Annual one-day IT infrastructure and cybersecurity conference with talks, panels and exhibitors, at the Spokane Convention Center.

organisations.name: INCH360 Cybersecurity & AI Conference
organisations.what: Free full-day regional cybersecurity and AI conference with regional and national speakers and CPE credit.

organisations.name: SAA Talks
organisations.what: Lunchtime speaker series from the Spokane Angel Alliance and Ignite Northwest at the Ignite Loft, featuring founders and investors.

organisations.name: Ignite 25+5 Awards
organisations.what: Annual recognition from Ignite Northwest and the Spokane Angel Alliance of the region's 25 most compelling emerging companies plus five startups to watch.

organisations.name: Sparks Weekend
organisations.what: Ignite Northwest's three-day pitch competition, successor to Startup Weekend Spokane, with a $50K investment prize, held at the Catalyst Building.

organisations.name: Business Brew
organisations.what: Informal early-morning coffee where business owners and founders put their questions to a business expert.

organisations.name: Spark Central
organisations.what: West Central nonprofit creative-learning centre with free high-speed internet, technology access, and robotics and coding programmes alongside arts and literary work.

organisations.name: Central Library studios & Business Lab
organisations.what: Spokane Public Library's downtown Central Library: three public media studios, a Maker Studio and a Business Lab for entrepreneurs. Home of StartUp Spokane.

organisations.name: The Lab at North Spokane Library
organisations.what: Spokane County Library District classroom and makerspace with a laser cutter, VR headsets and media-transfer equipment, open-hours access and STEM programmes.
organisations.cadence: Maker Open Hours on the SCLD calendar

organisations.name: Catalyst Building
organisations.what: Five-storey zero-energy building in the University District, home to EWU's computer science, engineering and cybersecurity labs, and a regular venue for ecosystem events and hackathons.

organisations.name: Spokane University District
organisations.what: 770-acre innovation district beside downtown, home to the WSU Health Sciences, EWU and Gonzaga campuses, with a life-science hub planned on the river.

organisations.name: Indaba Coffee (Broadway)
organisations.what: Hosts the Spokane Python User Group's Coffee & Code every first Monday at 7am.

organisations.name: Indaba Coffee (Summit)
organisations.what: Indaba describes its Kendall Yards location as being about "Farmer's Markets, local meet ups, and casual hang outs."

organisations.name: New Love Coffee (Kendall Yards)
organisations.what: Hosted the Spokane ACX Meetups Everywhere spring 2025 meetup.

organisations.name: New Love Coffee (Francis Ave)
organisations.what: Has a conference room that can be reserved in person, first come, first served.

organisations.name: New Love Coffee (Liberty Lake)
organisations.what: Has a reservable conference room and upstairs seating overlooking the river.

organisations.name: Atticus Coffee & Gifts
organisations.what: Downtown Spokane Partnership recommends it as a study spot for individuals or small groups of 4-5.

organisations.name: Jupiter's Eye Book Cafe
organisations.what: Downtown Spokane Partnership recommends it as a study spot for individuals or small groups of 3-4.

organisations.name: First Avenue Coffee
organisations.what: Downtown Spokane Partnership recommends it as a study spot for small to larger groups of 5-6.

organisations.name: Brews Bros Coffee Bar
organisations.what: Downtown Spokane Partnership recommends it as a study spot for individuals or small groups of 3-4.

organisations.name: Cedar Coffee
organisations.what: Visit Spokane noted its large back room where you can work or bring friends to study.

organisations.name: Arctos Coffee (Hamilton)
organisations.what: Visit Spokane listed it as an off-campus study spot about a half-mile walk from Gonzaga.

organisations.name: Little Garden Cafe (Waikiki)
organisations.what: Visit Spokane listed it as an off-campus study spot within walking distance of Whitworth University.

organisations.name: Eastern Coffee Roasters
organisations.what: Its West Plains Chamber listing shows wifi; the cafe is in the historic Cheney train depot.

organisations.name: Evans Brothers Coffee
organisations.what: Offers wifi and plenty of seating for studying.

organisations.name: Evans Brothers Coffee (Sandpoint Cafe + Roastery)
organisations.what: Named one of the six best study spots in Sandpoint, for its comfortable seating.

organisations.name: One World Cafe
organisations.what: Says its indoor and outdoor spaces are for people to work, study and socialize.

organisations.name: Neill's Coffee and Ice Cream
organisations.what: The owner calls it a place to use the wifi and get work done, and the Daily Evergreen says it has plenty of room for studying.

organisations.name: Thomas Hammer Coffee Roasters (Pullman)
organisations.what: Has big tables for groups who want to study and smaller tables for individuals.

organisations.name: Mela Coffee Roasting Company
organisations.what: Described by local radio as having the perfect vibe to take your homework to.

organisations.name: North Town Coffeehouse
organisations.what: Noted for great espresso, ambience and wifi in Yakima's historic train depot.

organisations.name: Carte Coffee
organisations.what: Visit Walla Walla calls it a great shop to camp out in, with outlets at every table and wifi.

organisations.name: Coffee Perk
organisations.what: Has solo and group study tables with outlets under each.

organisations.name: Novel Coffee Co.
organisations.what: Visit Tri-Cities describes it as perfect for studying or reading a good book.

organisations.name: Innovation Collective (Innovation Den)
organisations.what: Innovation Collective's Innovation Den fills a former Elks building with 34,000 sq ft of "startups, coffee, and collisions". It has housed 50+ companies and hosted 1,000+ entrepreneur events in 13 years of meeting twice a month. Current events are posted on Innovation Collective's Build_ platform (Build Cities). The 2017 conversion added offices, monthly coworking, a public coffee shop and an event hall seating about 170.
organisations.cadence: Entrepreneur events twice a month, per Innovation Collective; dates are listed on Build Cities.

organisations.name: SpaceShare CDA
organisations.what: Coeur d'Alene coworking desk memberships with 24/7 access, private offices, and bookable conference rooms for 6 or 12 people.

organisations.name: MosCoWork
organisations.what: Moscow's open-plan coworking space with 24/7 access, desks and private booths, fiber internet and a conference room, rented month to month.

organisations.name: The Plaza Downtown
organisations.what: Bonners Ferry flexible workspace offering shared desks and private offices with high-speed internet and meeting rooms.

organisations.name: Mercantile at Ellis-Forde
organisations.what: Mercantile's flagship downtown Wenatchee coworking space, with day and flex passes, fixed desks with 24/7 access, office suites, conference rooms and event space.

organisations.name: What is Crypto Currency (Crypto, Conspiracy Theories and Emerging Technologies)
organisations.what: A weekly round-table on blockchain, cryptocurrencies and emerging technologies, "Crypto Chatter" from 8 to 10am; no RSVP needed, and a core group attends every week.
